_comment: The perf rubric: the bands' thresholds and the letter rules. The single source for tools/perf/grade.py, tools/perf/grade.ts (the site computes the letter from a summary with it) and the test page (perf.js, to stop the ladder). docs/perf.md cites each source. Change on purpose, with the docs and the tests (test/grade-cases.json).
name: Clarity
_name: The perf test's name, as in "Clarity A" or "a frame's Clarity grade" (the maintainer, 2026-11-13). The report headline, the summary and grade.ts take it from here, so a rename is one change. File paths keep tools/perf and docs/perf.md.
_clarity: Clarity's version: v2 from rubric 2 (2026-11-14). Clarity v1 (protocol 1, rubric 1, 2026-11-14) was the first release; a v1 report or summary is graded only by v1's rules: re-measure under these. One without `clarity` was measured with a pre-release version (protocols 1 to 8, rubrics 1 to 11, before 2026-11-14): re-measure. Pre-release protocol 8 was v1's release candidate (#205, s1rtc5), so report.py reads its lines as v1.
_protocol: The measurement protocol these rules apply to (tools/perf/page/tiers.json PROTOCOL): the pages, the swipes, the update rate, the windows and how the runner reads them. A summary from another protocol can't be graded with this file: re-measure. Protocol 2 (Clarity v2, 2026-11-14) is protocol 1 plus the blocking time: the animation frames from each view's first screen drawn to usable. Protocol 1 (Clarity v1, 2026-11-14): Home Assistant's real frontend on a fake HA; a restart, then light, typical without its camera, typical with it, and heavy, each opened in the loaded frontend; live updates, taps and swipes on each; live cameras played over WebRTC, as HA with go2rtc does (over the LAN when the panel can reach the computer, else through adb reverse, and the run records which), graded on the receiver's own counts over a fixed 30 s window, with HLS copies as detail; each task its own budget. Its history (pre-release protocols 1 to 8 and rubrics 1 to 11, #158, #174, #202, #205) is in docs/perf.md, "Versions".

frame_p95_ms.source: web.dev RAIL (16 ms frame budget); Android vitals slow frame (> 16 ms). One and two frames at 60 Hz, plus 0.5 ms slack

frame_jank_pct.source: good: same as p95 within budget (derived); poor: Play Console 'excessive slow frames' (> 50% over 16 ms)

frame_frozen_pct.source: Android vitals frozen frame (> 700 ms); poor: Play Console 'excessive frozen frames' (> 0.1%); good 0%: project choice

load_ms.source: Core Web Vitals LCP bounds (good <= 2.5 s, poor > 4 s), applied to opening each reference view: since rubric 2, from HA's navigate() in the loaded frontend to the first screen drawn (every head card and every card on the screen rendered, stable for 2 frames, on screen), the paint LCP itself times. Rubric 1 ran to usable (drawn and the main thread free), stricter than LCP's paint; the main thread's work after the draw is now its own task, blocking_ms. Lenient for a view switch (docs/perf.md, Open the view)

inp_ms.source: Core Web Vitals INP (good <= 200 ms, poor > 500 ms), taps on each reference dashboard's toggle

start_ms.source: the restart (pre-release protocol 4): app process start to the reference dashboard's start view being usable, the kiosk having been pointed at it (before pre-release protocol 4: to engine ready, GeckoView's own first PageStart). poor: Android vitals' excessive cold start bound (>= 5 s), which vitals apply to TTID. good <= 2.5 s: project choice (LCP's bound)

blocking_ms.source: Lighthouse's Total Blocking Time bands for mobile (good 0-200 ms, poor above 600 ms; developer.chrome.com/docs/lighthouse/performance/lighthouse-total-blocking-time, read 2026-11-14), applied since rubric 2 to the main thread's blocking from each view's first screen drawn to usable (its main thread free for 500 ms): TBT's window is FCP to TTI. Gecko has no Long Tasks API (bugzil.la/1348405), so each animation frame's time past 50 ms counts, as a long animation frame's (stats.js frameBlocking). Graded as open is: good or needs-improvement passes every level, poor fails

js_burst_ms.source: project choice: one state burst fits in a frame; poor past RAIL's 50 ms input budget

grade._comment: The letter. Scroll and live updates are judged per run on their own levels (scroll_levels, update_levels: the first whose rule holds; `below` when none does), then the median level of the runs (the worse middle for an even count). Tap, load and start are bands of the median of the runs. A page is at a level when each task is one the level accepts. The first letter whose every page need holds is the grade, else the fallback. A restart in start_cap.band caps the letter at start_cap.letter (never raises it); letters rank by their place in this list. Frames bands are the worst of frame_p95_ms, frame_jank_pct and frame_frozen_pct.

scroll_levels._comment: the 60 fps rule: the frames band is good (p95 within one frame plus slack, jank <= 5%, no frozen frame)
average >= 50 fps over the swipes and p95 <= 50 ms: three frames at 60 Hz, plus the rubric's 0.5 ms slack
average >= 30 fps over the swipes and p95 <= 67 ms: four frames at 60 Hz (66.67 ms), plus the 0.5 ms slack

update_levels._comment: good, and the frames that had a change to draw hold the 60 fps bar (frames band good): a label, like scroll's
p95 of change to screen (a change reaches the page -> the first frame on screen that shows it) <= 100 ms
p95 of change to screen <= 200 ms

grade._camera: Live camera streams, played over WebRTC (#174, #202), on the pages in camera_pages; a page without streams is `none`, which every level accepts. Per run, the worst stream counts: its first frame, timed from the navigation, so it includes building the view; the share of its frames shown over the camera window (30 s from the view going live: frames / 15 fps x the time), its longest gap between frames and its stalls added up. Over WebRTC the frames, gaps and stalls are the receiver's own (getStats: framesDecoded; freezes, by libwebrtc's rule a gap of at least 3x the mean or the mean + 150 ms, at their full length; pauses; time in which nothing was decoded); without a freeze the longest gap is that rule's bound. Over HLS (the fallback, not graded) they are the video element's frame callbacks, with gaps over 500 ms as stalls. A stream that never showed a frame fails. Bars from #174's proposal, to be calibrated on the S1 before they're final.

camera_levels._comment: first frame within 2 s, at least 95% of frames shown, no stall over 500 ms
first frame within 4 s, at least 85% shown, stalls (gaps over 500 ms) under 1 s in all

letters._comment: an A where every task on heavy also holds 60 fps (the premium level)

letters.meaning: a good wall panel even for large dashboards
a good wall panel for typical dashboards, with a camera
letters._comment: typical with its camera playing, good. Each letter adds one page: D light, C typical without a camera, B typical with one, A heavy (2026-11-13)

letters.meaning: a good wall panel for typical dashboards without a camera
letters._comment: typical without its camera (a still picture in its place): the camera's cost is B's to judge (the maintainer, 2026-11-13)

letters.meaning: a good wall panel for light dashboards

fallback.meaning: not a good wall panel, even for light dashboards

grade._pages: The pages graded, lightest first. typical-nocam is typical with a still picture where its camera card was (tiers.json PLAIN); it has no camera task.
